title: The Spiritual Espousals
author: John of Ruysbroeck
description: The Spiritual Espousals (Die Gheestelike Brulocht) by Jan van Ruusbroec (John of Ruysbroeck, 1293-1381), the Flemish priest and contemplative of Groenendaal, here in an English translation of the 1940s-50s by Eric Colledge, made from the Ruusbroec-Genootschap critical edition (1932) and with introduction and bibliography. Ruusbroec's masterpiece, written in Middle Dutch around 1335, is structured around Christ's words 'See, the bridegroom comes; go out to meet him' (Matthew 25:6). Its three books describe three levels of life: the active life of virtue and moral striving, the interior or yearning life of devotion and union with God through grace, and the contemplative or 'God-seeing' life, in which the soul is united with God without intermediary in the dark, fruitful silence of the divine essence and the life of the Trinity. A classic of Low Countries mysticism, it influenced the Devotio Moderna, Tauler and later Catholic spirituality.
